_comment: Citation registry for Trail Mix. Every factual claim in history.json points at a source id here. Nothing renders educational text unless its source is present AND verified:true. See docs/asset-spec.md rule 18.

_schema.title: human-readable source name
_schema.verified: true only when a human has opened the URL and confirmed the claim

research_queue.subject: Sandviksbatteriet — construction period, purpose, armament, WWII use
research_queue.why_blocked: Web search now consistently returns 1898 (as part of Bergen's inner fortifications, built 1895-1905 alongside Kvarven and Hellen forts) and describes 24 cm L/13 M1898 St. Chamond howitzer positions still visible at the upper battery — corroborated across Bergen byleksikon, Norwegian Wikipedia and a hiking guide (2026-08-22 search pass). This is meaningfully stronger than the earlier conflicting hiking-site claims, but still only WebSearch-snippet-confirmed, not read in full by a human — bergenbyarkiv.no, snl.no, no.wikipedia.org and kulturminnesok.no remain unreachable from the build environment.

research_queue.subject: Neevengården/Sandviken sykehus — architect, opening-day capacity, construction timeline
research_queue.why_blocked: The name-change dates (1891/1927/1978) are already verified via snl_sandviken_sykehus. This is additional detail from a different source — Bergen byarkiv's own oppslagsverket entry — naming architect Ole F. Ebbell (Ole Falk Ebbel, 1839-1919), construction starting autumn 1887, completion 1 April 1891, and capacity for 178 patients across six patient buildings plus admin/economy/mortuary/farm buildings. Corroborated across two independent bergenbyarkiv.no pages, Bergen kommune's own history feature and Norwegian Wikipedia (2026-08-22 search pass), but bergenbyarkiv.no is unreachable from the build environment, so no human here has read the primary page.

research_queue.subject: Munkebotn valley and the Munken rock formation — the medieval boundary stream Gunnhildarå, Dominican monastery grazing, and the local legend attached to the monk-shaped rock
research_queue.why_blocked: Bergen byleksikon has a dedicated entry describing a real rock formation that can resemble a kneeling monk under certain light, with legends attached (including a version published in Bergens Tidende, 15 March 1980) — plus a separate entry on the Munkebotn valley itself naming the Gunnhildarå stream as Bergen's documented northern boundary until 1565, and Dominican-monastery grazing. Corroborated across bergenbyarkiv.no's own byleksikon and a Bergens Tidende article title (2026-08-22 search pass), but bergenbyarkiv.no is unreachable from the build environment.

research_queue.subject: Claimed connection between Fløyen and witch-trial-era 'trolldans' testimony
research_queue.why_blocked: A pasted research document claimed 'historical discussion also records stories of trolldans on Fløyen' tied to the 16th-century witch trials. A dedicated search pass (2026-08-22) found no independent source for this specific claim — only the well-documented Anne Pedersdotter case (Bergen, 1590), which this project's own folklore.json already reserves for a different route (Lyderhorn). Not used anywhere in this project unless a real, specific source for the Fløyen connection turns up.
try: a scholarly edition of the trial records
